title: dashboard browser command: agents claim tabs, read, screenshot, act, release
notes:
After the browser mode card merges. A dashboard command (like pane and board, not an MCP server; one call, short output) over the app's socket, driving only browser views through webContents.debugger (CDP). Never --remote-debugging-port: it would expose the app window and terminals.
Verbs (names to fit the command's style):
- open <url> [--project]: opens a new tab claimed by the calling pane; claim <tab> / release <tab>; tabs: list with holder and url. A pane may act only on tabs it holds; the user may take any tab back with a key (revoke), and the agent's next call on it is refused, saying so (errors-rule-1). A pane's tabs are released when its pane is released, finished or its agent exits.
- go <tab> <url>, back, reload; resize <tab> <width>x<height> (viewport emulation, for checking a layout at a phone width) and reset.
- read <tab> [--max-tokens n] [--selector css]: the page's main content as compact markdown (readability-style extraction, links kept short, scripts/styles/nav dropped), in the spirit of Agent Reach's reader (Jina Reader, --max-tokens) but local: page content behind logins never goes to a remote service. Report the token estimate it returned.
- screenshot <tab> [--full] [--element css]: saves a PNG and prints its path, so a worker can attach it to a PR.
- click / type / press on an element by a ref from a snapshot verb (the accessibility tree trimmed to interactive elements with short refs), and console / network: the last errors and failed requests.
- The calling pane is known from the environment the app gives panes; outside a pane, refuse.
Prompts: main's prompt and the work-card skill name the command in one line each. Docs: docs/browser. Tests for every decision module (claims, revoke, the reader's trimming).

comments.body: User requirement: engineer it properly, everything through actions (actions-rule-1; read docs/actions first). Every change of browser state is an action in src/main/actions/browser/ built with action() like the others: tab open, close, switch, navigate, back/reload, claim, release, revoke, resize/reset, and view show/hide/bounds. Every door calls those actions and nothing else: IPC handlers from the renderer, keys, the dashboard browser command's answers, and the sweeps that release a finished pane's tabs. No door touches a WebContentsView or webContents directly. Refusals are values ({ refused }, errors-rule-2) with the predicate exported where it is decided (errors-rule-1). Reads (read, screenshot, snapshot, console, network, tabs) may be queries, but go through one browser module, never a door's own code. bypasses.test.ts must not gain a count; add tests per action.
Runs alongside card 8d0d46ea (sign-in popups keep their opener), which changes the window.open path in browser-views.ts. Keep clear of it; merge main in when the other lands.
